newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht dips as overseas demand eases.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Baht dips as overseas demand eases.

text.p: * Thai baht eases as offshore demand subsides. Some bargain hunting interest in dollar seen at current levels.
* Singapore dollar firmer but off its highs on perceived central bank intervention after heavy overnight sales of Malaysian ringgit/Sing dollar cross.
* Malaysian ringgit slightly firmer on dollar sales by exporters and corporate interests.
* Indonesian rupiah steady as market seeks new leads with liquidity conditions providing sole point of interest.
The Thai baht shed some of its recent strength on Tuesday as demand abated in offshore markets, dealers said.
"Dollar selling (for baht) in offshore markets has eased. Some offshore players think it's an opportunity to buy the dollar at the current rate," a foreign bank dealer said.
"We may see a base forming for the dollar just below 24.00 baht for now," a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said.
Bangkok dealers said there was less selling pressure on the dollar in offshore markets as some foreign investors had acquired baht to cover short positions by selling Thai stocks late last week.
Thailand's two-tier baht system, imposed around mid-May to cut off baht supply to speculators, was expected to remain in place for a few months.

On Tuesday, the central Bank of Thailand (BOT) told local brokerages informally not to handle big lot stock transactions with foreigners in its latest move to cut offshore players' access to the baht, brokers said.
Senior BOT officials were not immediately available for comment.

The baht was quoted at 24.200/24.300 to the dollar at 0435 GMT in offshore markets against 24.150/24.250 late on Monday. In the domestic market, the baht was traded at 25.730/25.735 against 25.740/25.750 late on Monday.
The BOT lowered the baht/dollar midrate to 25.72 from 25.75 on Monday as the dollar weakened against the major currencies.

The Singapore dollar was off its highs, partly due to perceived intervention by the local monetary authority, after the domestic unit shot up against the U.S. dollar on heavy hedge fund sales of the ringgit/Sing cross overnight.
"Dollar/Sing traded to as low as 1.4170 last night. But this morning the central bank seems to be around," the U.S. bank dealer said.
"Local banks have been bidding aggressively around the 1.4200 level so we should see it remaining supported," he said.
The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), the de facto central bank, typically intervenes in forex markets through major local banks.
Dealers said the ringgit/Sing cross had fallen to an overnight low of 0.5635 as hedge funds, which were long, unloaded their positions.
"There was a big sell order on ringgit/Sing in London. When that happened dollar/Sing collapsed and dollar/ringgit shot up," a European bank dealer in Singapore.
The cross was quoted at 0.5663/70 at 0435 GMT and was seen trading within a new range of 0.5650-0.5675 for the time being.
The Malaysian ringgit firmed slightly against the U.S. dollar but dealers said its gains were limited by selling interest in the ringgit/Sing cross and activity was confined to a narrow range.
Another Singapore-based European bank dealer said there were some Malaysian exporters selling dollars at 2.5090 and speculators were picking up dollars around 2.5070.
"If the 2.5110 level holds for the next couple of days, then we should see dollar/ringgit moving down," the dealer said.

He said the selling of dollar/Sing was mainly by U.S. funds, which had built up positions in anticipation of the New York Commodities Exchange (NYCE) launching futures contracts on Asian currencies against the U.S. dollar.
The NYCE said on Monday it was delaying the launch of a Sing dollar futures contract, partly due to expressions of concern from the MAS.
"This is causing many to dump dollar/Sing," he said.
Futures contracts on the Thai baht, ringgit and Indonesian rupiah are expected to be launched on June 26.
Singapore has long restricted internationalisation of its currency and keeps a tight rein on trading of the Singapore dollar.
In Indonesia, the rupiah was relatively steady amid a dearth of fresh leads after the country's May 29 general election.
A U.S. bank dealer in Jakarta said offshore operators were still long on rupiah in the forward market although there were attempts to square positions at any opportunity.
She said many operators were also seen trying to establish fresh outright positions, keeping the market in range trading.
Spot rupiah was at 2,428.50/29.50 at 0435 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,429.0/29.5.
"Sentiment is mixed. There is no clear trend yet," a Japanese bank dealer said, adding that the market was desperate for fresh news after slowing down sharply in the past few days.
Dealers said rupiah liquidity was a bit tight, with overnight money traded at 12.0/13.0 percent, but attention was focused on the liquidity outlook for Friday.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221 384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662) 652-0642 and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
